desc:
prices[i] is the closing price of a stock on day i. The drawdown between two days i < j is prices[i] - prices[j], how far the price fell from day i to day j.

Return the largest drawdown over all pairs i < j. If the price never falls (or there is only one day), return 0.

Example: prices = [5,9,4,7,2,8] gives 7, the fall from 9 to 2.
hints: This is the mirror image of the classic 'best time to buy and sell' problem: instead of the biggest rise after a low, you want the biggest fall after a high.
For each day j, the best earlier day i is the one with the highest price so far.
Scan left to right, keep the running maximum price, and track the maximum of peak - price over all days.
editorial: For a fixed day j the largest drawdown ending at j is the highest earlier price minus prices[j]. So keep the highest price seen so far, peak, and for each day compute peak - prices[j]; the answer is the maximum of these values (and 0).

Comparing all pairs works but takes O(n^2). The single scan is O(n) time and O(1) space. Remember to update peak after (or together with) computing the drawdown; a day compared with itself contributes 0, so the order does not change the result.
